Definition: from a compound of G1119 and the alternate of G4098; to fall on the knee:--bow the knee, kneel down.
BiblicalUsage: gonypetéō means bow the knee, kneel down. In Matthew 17:14, the text says "kneeling down to him." In Matthew 27:29, the text says "and they bowed the knee before him."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gonypetéō shows us that worship is not a performance but a response — we answer what God has done with what we are. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Crucifixion; Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy; The Healing of the Demon-Possessed Boy
